answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, transferable token for a fixed period before it may submit bids or vote. Repeated identities then need repeated deposits, so an attacker must tie up real capital and forgo its yield; if identities misbehave, the protocol can slash the bond. This does not make Sybils impossible, but raises their cost in proportion to influence. A canyon of cheap accounts becomes a ripple of expensive commitments, with quartz tokens serving as the collateral.
